classification.difficultyReason: Both parts need algebraic expressions in x on every segment. Part a cancels x² terms in the chord product; part b uses the tangent-secant rule with whole secant x+5, then cancels x². Interpreting the segments and spotting the cancellation add demand.

answer.worked:
Intersecting chords have equal products of their intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+4)&=(x+1)(x+2)\\x^2+4x&=x^2+3x+2\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
The $x^2$ terms cancel.

The tangent squared equals the product of the external and entire secant lengths.
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)^2&=x(x+5)\\x^2+4x+4&=x^2+5x\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
The $x^2$ terms cancel.
